name: Grocery Checklist
description: A master grocery shopping list organized by aisle to make every trip faster and complete.

items.text: Leafy greens such as spinach, lettuce, or kale
Everyday vegetables: onions, carrots, peppers, broccoli

items.note: Buy only what you'll eat in a few days to avoid spoilage.

items.text: Ground beef, turkey, or a plant-based mince

items.note: Portion and freeze extra proteins the day you get home.

items.text: Frozen meals or pizza for busy nights
Nuts, trail mix, or granola bars
Trash bags and food storage bags

faq.q: How do I organize a grocery list by aisle?
faq.a: Group items into categories that match your store's layout, such as produce, dairy, pantry, proteins, and frozen. This lets you shop in one continuous loop instead of crisscrossing the store.

faq.q: How can a grocery checklist save me money?
faq.a: Shopping from a list curbs impulse buys, prevents duplicate purchases, and helps you buy only what you need for planned meals. Checking your pantry first avoids restocking items you already have.

faq.q: How often should I update my grocery list?
faq.a: Build a fresh list each week around your meal plan, but keep a running list on the fridge so you can jot down staples the moment they run low.

faq.q: Can I print this grocery checklist?
faq.a: Yes. You can print the checklist or download it as a PDF, then tick off each item as it lands in your cart.

faq.q: Should I shop the perimeter of the store first?
faq.a: Many shoppers start around the perimeter for fresh produce, dairy, and proteins, then move into the center aisles for pantry and packaged goods. This checklist is ordered to follow that flow.
